contract_plain_english: For every sub-gaussian random variable X, its psi_2 norm is the canonical size parameter for each of the four standard sub-gaussian bounds on printed page 27. Substituting ||X||_{psi_2} gives the stated tail, moment, square-exponential, and (when X is centered) MGF estimates with absolute constants and the displayed parameter ranges. Conversely, any positive scale that makes any one of those same forms valid must be at least a universal constant multiple of ||X||_{psi_2}; thus no characterization permits a substantially smaller scale. This is constant-factor minimality, not a claim that four sharp numerical optima are exactly equal.

binders: For each displayed characterization separately, a positive candidate scale K to be used in place of ||X||_{psi_2}.
t >= 0 in the tail characterization, p >= 1 in the moment characterization, and lambda in R in the MGF characterization.
conclusions: The scale ||X||_{psi_2} makes the tail inequality P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-c t^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) valid for all t >= 0, and any scale making that tail form valid cannot be smaller than ||X||_{psi_2} beyond an absolute constant factor.

The scale ||X||_{psi_2} makes the moment inequality ||X||_{L^p} <= C ||X||_{psi_2} sqrt(p) valid for all p >= 1, and any scale making that moment form valid cannot be smaller than ||X||_{psi_2} beyond an absolute constant factor.

The scale ||X||_{psi_2} makes E exp(X^2 / ||X||_{psi_2}^2) <= 2 valid, and a positive scale satisfying this normalized square-exponential inequality is bounded below by the defining infimum ||X||_{psi_2}.

If E X = 0, the scale ||X||_{psi_2} makes E exp(lambda X) <= exp(C lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2) valid for every lambda in R, and any scale making that centered-MGF form valid cannot be smaller than ||X||_{psi_2} beyond an absolute constant factor.
definitions_and_conventions: 'Up to absolute constant factors' asserts comparability of scales, not literal equality of their numerical optima.
The phrase 'each of these inequalities' refers separately to the four immediately preceding displays: (2.14), (2.15), the unnumbered square-exponential display, and (2.16).
hypotheses: X is sub-gaussian, meaning that it satisfies the equivalent properties i--iv referred to in Proposition 2.5.2.
Only for the MGF characterization, E X = 0.
A candidate K is being compared within the same displayed form of the selected inequality, with positive absolute constants.
implicit_context: The probability, expectation, and L^p norm are all taken for the same random variable X on its underlying probability space.
The constants called absolute do not depend on X or on the running parameter t, p, or lambda.
The four displayed estimates are a restatement of the equivalences in Proposition 2.5.2 in terms of the sub-gaussian norm.

details: Minimality is asserted for each of the four displayed inequalities individually.
A sufficient scale for any selected displayed characterization is comparable from below to ||X||_{psi_2}, while ||X||_{psi_2} itself is sufficient up to the displayed absolute constants.
The tail estimate is uniform over all t >= 0.
The moment estimate is uniform over all p >= 1.
The MGF estimate, when X is centered, is uniform over all lambda in R.
The hypothesis E X = 0 modifies the MGF display (2.16), not the tail, moment, or square-exponential displays.
The tail exponent has the negative quadratic ratio -c t^2/||X||_{psi_2}^2 and the leading factor 2.
The moment bound grows as sqrt(p).
The MGF exponent is quadratic in both lambda and the scale.
Equation (2.13) gives an infimum with the fixed threshold 2 for the square-exponential condition.
The following prose claims only constant-factor minimality across the four characterizations.

undebatable_constraints: The contract concerns the sentence after (2.16) on printed page 27 and the four inequalities immediately preceding it.
All four displayed characterizations must be covered separately; none may be omitted or merged into a different assertion.
The tail, moment, and MGF parameter ranges are respectively t >= 0, p >= 1, and lambda in R.
The condition E X = 0 applies to the MGF characterization only.
Minimality is up to absolute constant factors, except that the defining square-exponential condition directly yields the infimum comparison at threshold 2.
The probability tail is two-sided through |X|, the moment rate is sqrt(p), and both the tail and MGF exponents are quadratic in their running parameters and in the scale as displayed.
The psi_2 norm is the scale being characterized; it must not be conflated with a tail threshold t, a moment index p, an MGF parameter lambda, or an absolute constant.
